title: Single-residue engineering of Klenow fragment enables broad acceptance of chemically modified nucleotides.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Downloaded the complete supplement (1.57 MB zip holding one 1.93 MB, 30-page PDF) and extracted its text: Supplementary Table 1 = 7 mutagenesis primer pairs, Table 2 = 22 primer/template oligonucleotides, Table 3 = a list of ~24 nucleoside triphosphate abbreviations with drawn structures, Table 4 = 44 chimeric product sequences (lanes a-k x 34/63 nucleotide x DNA/RNA primer) with no numbers. Also pulled the article full-text XML: it contains exactly one table (Table 1, 8 steady-state kinetic rows = 2 enzymes x 4 nucleotides, with units s^-1, micromolar, M^-1 s^-1), licence CC BY-NC.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: The percentage extension yields (85-124%) and the error rate of 1.19 x 10^-3 are quoted in the running text and read off gel images (Supplementary Figs 1-16); no table of yields exists in the files. Molecular dynamics trajectories and gel densitometry raw values are not deposited anywhere I could find (no GEO/SRA/BioProject links, no Zenodo/Dryad hit on the DOI, and the two PDB codes found by text mining, 8OO6 and 1KFD, are pre-existing structures used as simulation starting models, not new depositions).

a1_downloadable.note: Open access (CC BY-NC); I downloaded the whole supplement without a login. But it is one PDF, not data: no repository deposit exists.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: FAIL: no label column anywhere. Extension yields live in prose sentences and gel photographs; anyone modelling this would have to transcribe numbers from text and re-quantify gel bands by hand, i.e. construct the target.

a3_inputs_present.note: Inputs are present: all primer/template sequences in Supplementary Tables 2 and 4, and nucleotide structures drawn in Table 3 (as images, so SMILES strings would have to be written out).

a4_units_stated.note: Table 1 states units explicitly (kcat in s^-1, Km in micromolar, kcat/Km in M^-1 s^-1), triplicate means with standard deviations.

a5_enough_rows.note: FAIL and decisive: 8 kinetic rows in the only table, plus roughly 40-60 percentage yields quoted in text across 5 mutants (E710A, F762A, F762Y, Y766S, E710A+F762A) and about 10 nucleotide systems. The checklist needs about 1,500 rows, or 400 for classification.

a6_fits_laptop.note: Trivially small; the whole supplement is under 2 MB.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: The one table and the text agree; there is no dataset whose row count could disagree, so this check is vacuous here.

a8_label_provenance.note: Labels are real physical measurements - denaturing gel band quantification and Michaelis-Menten fits - not another model's output. Provenance is the one thing this paper is clean on.

existing_models.name: Computational evolution of poly(U) polymerase (ESM1v protein language model embeddings + multilayer perceptron classifier, with Gaussian accelerated molecular dynamics; PMC12848935, 2026)
existing_models.score_and_split: Reported classification accuracy 0.67 for active/inactive variants and a 47.78% hit rate for designed variants; split not stated. Known only from the search-result summary - I did not open the paper.

existing_models.name: MutCompute (structure-based machine learning used to guide T7 RNA polymerase engineering)
existing_models.score_and_split: Used to nominate beneficial mutations in published T7 RNA polymerase campaigns; no number on a held-out split seen. From search-result summary only.

existing_models.name: EnzyACT (deep learning predictor of the effect of single and multiple mutations on enzyme activity)
existing_models.score_and_split: Benchmarked on curated mutation datasets; numbers not seen. From search-result summary only.

backbone.name: ESM-2 (protein language model) for the polymerase sequence plus ChemBERTa (molecule language model) for the triphosphate substrate
backbone.hardware: Laptop CPU would be ample for 5 enzyme variants
backbone.licence: ESM-2 MIT, ChemBERTa permissive - irrelevant here because there is no training set

integration.partner_dataset: No workable partner. A polymerase-variant activity table would be the thing to join to, and no public resource collects measured modified-nucleotide incorporation across polymerase mutants; UniProt/PDB only give the wild-type sequence and structure.
integration.join_key: UniProt P00582 (E. coli DNA polymerase I) + residue number
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Cannot be written from this paper alone: with 5 variants there is nothing to join that would answer a question neither source answers.

controls.positive_control: Would be the textbook fact that unmodified dATP is incorporated far better than any 2'-modified analogue (Table 1 shows 0.26 x 10^6 versus about 10^3 M^-1 s^-1), which any model must recover.
controls.negative_control: Label shuffling is meaningless at n=8.
controls.external_validation: None available: no second dataset of matched polymerase-variant/modified-nucleotide yields exists that I could find.

honest_claim_h3: With these files a model could claim nothing beyond 'one phenylalanine-to-alanine substitution in Klenow fragment raises catalytic efficiency for three specific nucleotide analogues', which is the paper's own measured result, not a prediction.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use enzyme sequence and nucleotide chemistry to predict whether a DNA-copying enzyme will accept a chemically modified building block.
plain_idea.train_on: What I considered: for each (polymerase variant, modified nucleotide) pair, the enzyme's amino acid sequence plus the nucleotide's chemical structure. This paper supplies 5 variants of one enzyme and about 10 nucleotide systems - roughly 50 pairs, verified by reading the supplement.
plain_idea.predict: The measured extension yield (percent of primer extended to full length on a denaturing gel) or catalytic efficiency kcat/Km from Michaelis-Menten fits. Truth comes from gel densitometry and kinetic assays run in this one laboratory.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Groups making xeno nucleic acid (XNA) therapeutics and aptamers now find useful polymerase mutants by trial-and-error directed evolution; a predictor would tell them which substitutions to build first. Even a failed model would map how little public data on this exists.

more_or_better_data.why: Our would-be dataset is about 50 hand-transcribed measurements on one enzyme; the poly(U) polymerase machine learning study trained on its own purpose-built variant library and language-model embeddings from millions of proteins.

confidence_score.why: Triplicate standard deviations exist for the 8 kinetic rows only, which is far too few points to calibrate per-prediction uncertainty.

models_beatable.why: Irrelevant: with 5 enzyme variants there is no held-out set on which to beat anything, and the 2026 poly(U) polymerase workflow already couples language-model predictions to its own wet-lab loop.

guaranteed_improvement.why: Fails the first condition - there is no baseline model for this exact task that could be run, and no dataset of matched measurements to add.

ml_idea: Considered and rejected: predict modified-nucleotide acceptance (extension yield or kcat/Km) for polymerase point mutants from an ESM-2 embedding of the mutant sequence plus a ChemBERTa embedding of the triphosphate. The paper provides only 5 Klenow variants and about 50 enzyme-substrate measurements, none of them in a machine-readable table, so the task cannot be set up from this source. The idea would need a purpose-built deep mutational scan of a polymerase against modified nucleotides, or a curation effort across dozens of XNA-polymerase papers, to become viable.

effort.compute_note: Estimated, not timed beyond the downloads I ran: the entire supplement is one 1.93 MB PDF, so all cost is manual transcription of numbers out of prose and gel figures (about 6 hours), and 5 sequences through ESM-2 on a CPU takes seconds.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Count the labelled measurements in the supplement - I did this: 8 kinetic rows in the only table, about 40-60 yields quoted in text, 5 enzyme variants. That kills it in ten minutes.

verdict_reason: Verified in the files: no dataset exists. The whole supplement is one 30-page PDF whose four tables hold primers, templates, nucleotide names and 44 product sequences; the only numeric table in the paper has 8 kinetic rows, and the extension yields sit in prose and gel photographs. Fails A2 (the label would have to be built by transcribing text and re-reading gels) and fails A5 by two orders of magnitude (about 50 measurements across 5 enzyme variants versus the 1,500-row bar). Excellent enzymology, no machine-learning substrate.
